title: A report on digitised neuronal tracing method to study neurons in their entirety
author: Ali, Sivakumar, et al.
materials: Animals: Seven healthy male albino rats of Wistar strain (6 months of age), weighing 250–300 g, were obtained from Central Animal Research Facility (CARF), Manipal Academy of Higher Education, after receiving approval from the Institutional Animal Ethics Committee (IAEC/KMC/106/2016). Rats were housed in polypropylene cages measuring 41 cm × 28 cm × 14 cm. They were maintained in a 12:12 hour Light: Dark environment, in an air-conditioned room and were fed with water and standard food ad libitum. All animals were kept under stress-free conditions prior to euthanisation. After euthanisation, brain was carefully dissected out, stained with Golgi-Cox as described earlier [20,21]. Six neurons per rat were selected, and a total of 42 neurons were digitally reconstructed or manually traced and analysed.

steps.title: Obtain and house experimental rats
steps.instruction: Acquire seven healthy male albino Wistar rats (6 months old, 250–300 g) from the Central Animal Research Facility, house them in polypropylene cages (41 cm × 28 cm × 14 cm) under a 12 h light/12 h dark cycle in an air‑conditioned room, and provide water and standard food ad libitum until euthanasia.

steps.title: Euthanise and Golgi‑Cox stain brains
steps.instruction: Euthanise each rat under stress‑free conditions, carefully dissect out the brain, and stain the tissue with Golgi‑Cox using the previously published protocol (references 20, 21).

steps.title: Capture serial photomicrographs (digitised method)
steps.instruction: Using a Motic BA210 widefield microscope equipped with a Moticam‑580 high‑resolution camera and Image Plus 2.0 MK software, acquire photomicrographs of each Golgi‑Cox‑stained CA3 neuron at ∼2 µm intervals along the z‑axis from appearance to disappearance; save images as TIFF files.

steps.title: Create image stack and trace neurons digitally
steps.instruction: Import the TIFF series into FIJI, stack the images along the axis perpendicular to the image plane to generate a single 3‑D image file, then open the file in Simple Neurite Tracer software and manually trace each of the 42 neurons (6 per rat), spending approximately 15–20 min per neuron.

steps.title: Calibrate camera‑lucida microscope
steps.instruction: Place a stage micrometer on the simple compound microscope attached to the camera‑lucida; set 1 mm = 100 divisions = 1000 µm. Verify that the distance between two major lines equals 100 µm, between a major line and an adjacent minor line equals 10 µm, and between a major line and the second minor line equals 20 µm.

steps.title: Manually trace neurons with camera‑lucida
steps.instruction: Identify each of the 42 previously imaged CA3 neurons, adjust the microscope X‑ and Y‑coordinates, and trace at 400× magnification using a laser‑tipped pencil; set the fine‑adjustment knob to move 0.002 mm per division and repeatedly shift focus back and forth to confirm that traced dendrites belong to the same neuron, spending about 30–45 min per neuron.

steps.title: Perform statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Calculate mean ± SE for apical and basal dendritic intersections and branching points per rat for each method, compare the two methods using an independent Student’s t‑test (p ≤ 0.05 considered significant), and conduct the analysis with SPSS software.
